title: A smooth section component propagates along specialization over a noetherian base
statement: Let g:P→T be smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with T noetherian and a section σ satisfying σ≫g=id. If y specializes to x and x lies in the connected component of σ(g(x)) in g⁻¹({g(x)}), then y lies in the connected component of σ(g(y)) in g⁻¹({g(y)}).

proof.text: The source is noetherian, since g is finitely presented over a noetherian base. Equality of the two points is immediate. Otherwise trace the specialization y⤳x by a discrete valuation ring using Tag 054F.

Base change g and σ to this trait. The tracing morphism gives a second section τ. Tag 055M identifies both component memberships with those upstairs. The special point of τ belongs to the component of the original section.

Remove the other special-fibre components. They are closed in the total space, so the complement is open. Both sections factor through it, since their special points lie in the chosen component and every open of the trait containing its closed point is the whole trait. The special fibre is connected.

The noetherian total space has finitely many open and closed connected components. The component containing the original section contains the entire special fibre and also the second section. It is flat with reduced special fibre, since it is an open in a smooth scheme over the trait. Tag 055J gives connected generic fibre.
The two generic section points therefore lie in the same component of the original generic fibre. Tag 055M transports this membership back to y.
